Metric series reference (MetricsQL)

Every series name the collectors write into the local metrics store, with its labels and products, plus working MetricsQL examples for Analytics panels.

👤 ForOperatorAdvanced user
🔑 Permissionsmonitoring.view
📍 WhereUsed in Monitoring → Analytics panels with "Store selector — MetricsQL"

What is it?#

A list of the series the collectors write, so you can write MetricsQL expressions for Analytics boards. MetricsQL is the query language of the VictoriaMetrics store; it is a superset of PromQL. Every series carries at least the labels device (appliance name) and kind (fortiweb, fortiadc, fortianalyzer, fortiauthenticator).

Health of collection itself#

Series Labels Meaning
satom_scrape_up device, kind, collector 1 when the target's last run succeeded, 0 when it failed. Written on every run

Box resources (box collector)#

Series Products Meaning
satom_box_cpu_pct FortiWeb, FortiADC, FortiAuthenticator CPU used, %
satom_box_mem_pct FortiWeb, FortiADC, FortiAuthenticator memory used, %
satom_box_disk_pct FortiWeb, FortiAuthenticator disk used, %
satom_box_logdisk_pct FortiWeb log disk used, %
satom_box_sessions FortiWeb concurrent sessions
satom_box_conn_per_sec FortiWeb new connections per second
satom_box_mem_used_bytes, satom_box_mem_total_bytes, satom_box_disk_used_bytes, satom_box_disk_total_bytes FortiAuthenticator absolute memory and disk

Published services (policies, vservers, traffic, transactions)#

Label policy = FortiWeb server policy or FortiADC virtual server name.

Series Products Meaning
satom_policy_up FortiWeb, FortiADC 1 when the appliance reports the service's status as up / enabled / running, else 0
satom_policy_sessions FortiWeb, FortiADC concurrent sessions
satom_policy_conn_per_sec FortiWeb, FortiADC connections per second
satom_policy_client_rtt_ms, satom_policy_server_rtt_ms, satom_policy_app_response_ms FortiWeb (per policy) latency, ms. FortiADC writes its device-wide values as satom_adc_*_ms instead (below)
satom_policy_count FortiWeb, FortiADC number of published services on the device (no policy label)
satom_policy_throughput_bps, satom_policy_throughput_peak_bps FortiWeb (traffic, top N) per-policy throughput
satom_total_throughput_bps, satom_total_throughput_peak_bps FortiWeb (traffic) device total throughput
satom_policy_transactions_window FortiWeb (transactions, top N) HTTP transactions in the window

FortiADC device counters (vservers)#

satom_adc_sessions, satom_adc_sessions_limit, satom_adc_sessions_total, satom_adc_requests_total, satom_adc_request_errors_total, satom_adc_response_errors_total, satom_adc_in_bytes_total, satom_adc_out_bytes_total; device-wide latency in ms: satom_adc_client_rtt_ms, satom_adc_server_rtt_ms, satom_adc_app_response_ms (no policy label — FortiADC does not report latency per virtual server); pool health: satom_pool_member_up (labels pool, member), satom_pool_member_count, satom_pool_member_down.

Interfaces (interfaces)#

Label iface. satom_iface_up (1 = link up), satom_iface_rx_bytes_total, satom_iface_tx_bytes_total (cumulative counters — use rate()).

FortiAuthenticator (capacity, identity)#

Series Labels Meaning
satom_fac_licence_used, satom_fac_licence_total, satom_fac_licence_pct resource licensed seats
satom_fac_token_used, satom_fac_token_total, satom_fac_token_pct pool FortiToken pools
satom_fac_ha_peer — HA peer present
satom_fac_inventory resource directory object counts
satom_fac_inventory_failed — number of inventory reads that failed

FortiAnalyzer (faz)#

Series named satom_faz_<signal> with a resource label, where <signal> is one of logstats, storage, logfiles, alerts, incidents, devices, tasks; plus satom_faz_signals_failed. No log body is ever fetched.

Example expressions#

satom_box_cpu_pct                                   # every device, one line each
topk(10, satom_policy_conn_per_sec)                 # the ten busiest services
sum by (device) (satom_policy_up == 0)              # services down, per device
rate(satom_iface_rx_bytes_total[5m]) * 8            # interface bandwidth, bit/s
sum by (collector) (satom_scrape_up == 0)           # failing collectors
satom_fac_licence_total - satom_fac_licence_used    # free licence seats
satom_box_cpu_pct{device=~"$device"}                # filtered by a board variable

$device and $policy work only on boards that define those variables (for example the built-in Device drill-down and Service drill-down boards).

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: FortiADC device-wide RTT and application response time are stored as satom_adc_client_rtt_ms, satom_adc_server_rtt_ms and satom_adc_app_response_ms; the satom_policy_* latency series are now strictly per FortiWeb policy. Update custom panels that queried the old names for FortiADC; history already recorded under the old names stays there.

Troubleshooting#

"The store rejected that expression: …"#

Shown when you save a panel: SATOM runs the expression against the store before saving it and the store refused it. Check the syntax and series names above.

A FortiADC latency panel stopped updating#

The panel queries satom_policy_client_rtt_ms (or the server-RTT / app-response twin) for a FortiADC. Those values are now written as satom_adc_client_rtt_ms, satom_adc_server_rtt_ms and satom_adc_app_response_ms; edit the panel's expression.

A panel shows an error instead of a chart#

The store is down or the query failed; a failed query is never drawn as an empty chart. Check the store status on Collection.
